name: Sliding window + counting array
space: O(128): one counter per ASCII character
whenToUse: The standard answer. s is ASCII, so a counting array of 128 works; for any Unicode text you would use a hash map instead.

card.signals: "substring" (contiguous), "without duplicate characters" (a rule every window must keep) and "longest". If a window has a repeat, every bigger window that contains it has the repeat too, so you can grow on the right and shrink on the left.
card.pattern: a variable-size window. Each index enters the window once (right) and leaves at most once (left), so the whole scan is O(n).
card.coreIdea: add s[right] to count. Only s[right] can be a repeat, so move left to the right until its old copy is gone. Then the window is unique: compare its length with longest.

invariant: After each shrink loop, the window s[left..right] has no repeated character, and count holds how often each character is in it.
